region.text: the Hejaz land that the Ottoman ledger/164 takes in 1812 but the Ottoman shape of 1812-1813 does not hold: the Mecca, Jeddah and Taif country, Saudi until 1813-1814

events.note: Gives back what ledger/164 over-takes. Ledger/164 hands the Ottoman Empire all of the Hejaz inside its 1815 shape in 1812, but the Ottoman 1812-1813 keyframe holds only part of it, so the 1812 snap empties about 600 Hejaz cells to nobody (and the 1812 Saudi keyframe, which drops Yanbu, Medina, Jeddah and Mecca, cannot hold them either). The page: Mecca fell in January 1813, Jeddah 'a month later' than Medina (late 1812), Taif in 1814; 'the five major cities of Western Arabia (Hejaz) had returned to Ottoman rule' only after the first campaign; the treaty of 1815 made the Wahhabis 'give up Hijaz'. The cities are moved to Muhammad Ali's account by the emirate's ledger/19-22 in their own years; the rest of the Saudi Hejaz stays Saudi to the spring of 1815 (emirate's ledger/23).

region.text: the Duchy of Warsaw less the western parts that went to Prussia (Grand Duchy of Posen) and the Free City of Krakow

events.note: 9 June 1815: the Final Act of the Congress of Vienna creates the Kingdom of Poland out of most of the Duchy of Warsaw. The Russian ledger/65 gives the whole of 'Congress Poland' to the Russian Empire as direct land in the same year and, applied first, leaves the kingdom's own founding (ledger/0) only 46 cells; the kingdom then shows as a speck inside direct Russian land. The page: 'The Congress Kingdom of Poland was created out of the Duchy of Warsaw'; 'the Polish Kingdom in its 1815 form was a semi-autonomous state in a personal union with Russia', with 'the Constitution of the Kingdom of Poland' and 'an independent army'; its autonomy was abolished only after 1831 and the Organic Statute of 1832. This hands the kingdom its land back from the Russian Empire, where data/colonies.csv draws it in the Russian vassal tint.

region.text: the Karabakh, Shirvan and Shaki khanates, which Persia recognised as Russian at Gulistan

events.note: 24 October 1813: the war ends and the khanates are Russian. The page: 'Persia recognized Russian possession of all the khanates it held and gave up all pretensions to Dagestan and Georgia'; 'The border in the northern part of Talysh was left for later decision.' Ledger/60-62 close the khanates' vassal relations, whose land belongs to no dossier, so it drops to nobody (about 215 cells of Azerbaijan stay grey from late 1813 to the 1814 shape), and ledger/63's gain takes only land held by the Qajar state. This gives the khanate land to the Russian Empire in the month the vassal relations end.

region.text: whatever of Spain Joseph's state still holds in June 1813

events.note: June 1813: Joseph's state has no land left. The page: 'Joseph permanently left Spain in June'; 'French troops were finally evicted from Spain following the conclusion of the Siege of San Sebastian in September 1813'. Bonapartist Spain's ledger/10 and /12 hand over only (the 1814 shape minus the 1812 shape), so about 190 cells that Joseph held inside the 1812 shape (La Mancha, Jaen, Granada, Murcia, Valencia, Leon) are still his when its 1813 keyframe, which leaves them out, snaps them to nobody; they stay grey to the end of 1813 and return with the 1814 Spanish shape. The successor of Bonapartist Spain is the Kingdom of Spain (its identity.successors). The cells the French held themselves (Catalonia, and Biscay, Navarre and Aragon until June) are not Joseph's and are left alone.

region.text: Ñuble north of the Biobio and the Los Lagos region of Osorno, Llanquihue and Chiloe

rulings.why: The independent Mapuche country lay south of the Biobio: settlers later advanced 'from the north across Bio Bio River into Mapuche territory', and Sarmiento's line puts the unclaimed land 'between two Chilean provinces (Concepcion and Valdivia)'. Chiloe stayed Spanish: the Spanish were expelled from the archipelago only in 1823 and later (Arauco War: Chiloe the one Spanish-held land south of the Biobio). The Mapuche keyframe reaches into Ñuble and the Los Lagos region; the size rule gives those cells to the Mapuche in 1810-1817 (about 80 cells a year).

region.text: the Dutch islands of the Moluccas, Ambon, Ternate and Banda

rulings.why: Territorial evolution of the British Empire: 'Java and the Spice Islands | 1811-1816 | Occupied | restored to the Netherlands'. The dossiers of both states carry the occupation (dutch-east-indies ledger/12 and /20), but Cliopatria drops the British shape's Moluccas in 1814, the year of the treaty, and the size rule gives the cells to the Dutch as plain land in 1814-1815; they were British-occupied Dutch land until 1816.

The Hejaz was Saudi land until the Ottoman-Egyptian campaign: 'Wahhabi forces led by Abdulaziz bin Muhammad Al Saud entered Mecca in 1803'; 'the Wahhabis gained control of Mecca and Medina by 1805'; only after the first campaign (landing at Yanbu in 1811, Medina in late 1812, Jeddah and Mecca in January 1813) 'the five major cities of Western Arabia (Hejaz) had returned to Ottoman rule', and the treaty of 1815 made the Wahhabis 'give up Hijaz'. Habesh Eyalet's keyframe draws the coastal Hejaz as Ottoman for the whole of 1557-1864, so R1 (colony wins) hands the emirate's Hejaz keyframes (1,393 cells in 1811, 911 in 1812) to the Ottoman tint while Diriyah's own ledger events (Yanbu 1811, Medina 1812, Jeddah and Mecca 1813) find nothing to take. Years 1814-1815 are left to R1: the Ottomans held the cities by then and Cliopatria's Saudi shapes of those years are too wide. Seam: the same ruling is needed for 1803-1810 in the window p1800-p1809, or the Hejaz flips from Ottoman to Saudi on 1 January 1811.
